vpn1049-about.text:
Apple's cancel screen (Retention Messaging). App Store Connect → the subscription group → Retention Messaging; drafts made in VPN-1019, nothing live.
Where: the user taps Cancel Subscription in the App Store's subscription settings (iPhone, iPad, Mac with macOS 14+). Apple draws the whole screen; we give a header, a text and one image (or an offer).
Who sees the image: only when no offer shows. M3 (Yearly, 6-month): always. M1 (Weekly), M2 (Monthly): users who cannot get the offer: trial users, less than 1 paid month, Kuwait, an offer in the last 6 months. Most viewers are trial users who cancel (about 246 a week, mostly the Gulf and Jordan).
One image for all 3 messages: it has no words, so English and Arabic readers see the same image; the three messages share one promise (a private connection on every network), so there is nothing to show per plan. Apple allows only one image per message, the same for every language.
What it is: the app's splash, in 16:9. The app's page background (gradient-background #172231 → #000000, corner to corner, with World-Map.png in overlay blend, as GradientBackground.swift) and the splash logo (Lotties/Logo.json, last frame, rendered as vector at 50 % of the width, centred). Users know it from every app start. No prices, no offer marks, no words except the SecureField word-mark, no part of Apple's screens.
File: design-paywalls/assets/retention/SecureField-RetentionMessage-3840x2160.png · 3840 × 2160 · PNG, RGB, no alpha channel · 2.5 MB. SecurefieldiOS adds it to M1, M2 and M3 after the board approves. Apple's alt text: not asked for in App Store Connect (the API needs it: "SecureField").
